description:
verify.rs:415-424: the loop calls `verify_sct_for_precert` for each SCT in the list. Each call invokes `tbs_without_sct_list(leaf_der)` (verify.rs:963-990) which: parses the cert, mutates, re-encodes the TBS. It also invokes `issuer_key_hash_from_cert(issuer_der)` which: parses the cert, re-encodes the SPKI, SHA-256s it.

Both results are invariant across SCTs (they depend only on leaf_der and issuer_der, not on the SCT). Computing them once before the loop, then passing the byte buffers into a per-SCT helper, eliminates O(N) redundant cert parses and re-encodes.

Expected impact: typical CT-logged TLS certs carry 2-3 embedded SCTs, so this saves 1-2× cert-parse-and-reencode per call. Not catastrophic, but the cost class is wrong — a cert-parse-and-reencode is hundreds of microseconds; CT verification gets called per-TLS-handshake in some deployments. At a CDN's hundreds of thousands of handshakes per second, 'redundant cert parse per SCT' becomes a measurable hot-spot.

Fix: hoist the two computations outside the loop. Internal helper accepting `tbs_no_sct: &[u8]` and `issuer_key_hash: &[u8; 32]` already exists (`build_signed_input_precert_entry` takes them). `verify_sct_for_precert` can stay as the public single-SCT entry point; `verify_embedded_scts` calls a hoisted-cached internal helper.
title: verify_embedded_scts re-runs tbs_without_sct_list / issuer_key_hash per SCT — O(N) DER work
